newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures drop on rate report, U.S. missiles.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures drop on rate report, U.S. missiles.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures dropped on Tuesday as fears of a rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve were reignited by a newspaper report.
The Wall Street Journal reported in its Tuesday edition that Fed policy makers are considering a bigger-than-expected interest rate increase.
The fears were further fuelled by news just before the close that the United States had launched cruise missiles against military targets in Iraq.
The December contract ended 0.13 down at 120.49. Turnover was 69,966 contracts.

Some dealers said the December contract was also lifted by a report in the Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a major Japanese financial daily, which said that the Japanese government may not make a supplementary budget this autumn.

Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said he agreed with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that the cabinet would make a final decision on the budget after Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data due out in mid-September.

The remarks prompted the quick sale of what had been bought on the Nihon Keizai Shimbun article, another trust bank dealer said. The Nikkei 225 stock index also became unfriendly to bonds after climbing back above the 20,000 level.
These two factors combined pushed back the December contact close to its Monday level by early afternoon, dealers said.
In late afternoon, the December's fall was accelerated by the report about a possible rate hike by the Fed. News of the launch of U.S. cruise missiles against Iraq dealt the market another blow.
In the cash bond market, medium-term JGBs were notably weak. Dealers said the day's easing was a correction of a recent rapid uptrend.
Some dealers also said that some of the sales would be related to profit-taking before many Japanese firms' first-half book closings at the end of September.
Dealers said such activities are common, particularly when stocks are not in good shape.
The benchmark 182nd 10-year JGBs were yielding 2.990 percent, up 0.040 from Monday, as of 0743 GMT.
